decisions.reason: The source also changes the Big Block winner count and sales trigger, but a complete same-message MODIFY already represents that impact.
The FAQ's current prize-block description contains the superseded winner counts and draw frequencies and must reflect the new Small and Big Block parameters.

source_message.speaker: client
source_message.text:
I just had a thought.... I think we need to tweak the block prizes to
- Small = 1 x $500 every 100 sales.
- Big = 1 x $10,000 every 10,000 sales.

Same net $ amount given away but smoother, cleaner, clearer and more consistent stream of winners

value_updates.prize_block_description: Small Block awards 1 × $500 every 100 mint or secondary sales; Big Block awards 1 × $10,000 every 10,000 mint or secondary sales; pools are funded from every sale forever.

decisions.reason: Changing prize winner counts and sales-based draw frequencies does not change which sale types fund the prize pools or the funding duration.
The source changes prize amounts and draw frequencies, but it does not change ticket counters, eligibility windows, weighting, or post-draw reset behavior.
The number and frequency of prizes change, while random Chainlink VRF selection, ticket weighting, fairness, and verification remain unchanged.
The no-referral recipient rule and its commission and ticket awards remain valid despite the changed prize draw parameters.
The source does not resolve or alter whether prizes are paid automatically or claimed through the Winners page.
A successful coded referral still awards the same commission and one Small and one Big Block ticket.
Both Small and Big Block ticket counters remain required in NFT metadata; only the associated prize draw parameters change.
The source does not change the requirement for a flat $10 secondary-sale royalty.
The NFT mint number remains the permanent referral code with the same display locations.
The revised schedules preserve the stated net prize amount per sale and do not change mint price, founder share, referral commission, or prize-pool funding.
